notes:
Round-1 standard applied: a rule the old routing table also did not route the task to is not counted as a split defect - e.g. menu.md's 'Never present a heavier option as better' is not routed for a worded 'catch up' (row 67); item 20's own cumulative tiers, its question and its Bounded default carry the substance.
Compaction margin: SKILL.md's first part ends at 20,052 characters, exactly 20,480 bytes; at a strict 20,000-character window the override paragraph would lose '...age against a copy that could have gone stale (§10).' Set aside: the window is only described as about 20,000 characters, and the rule is restated in §10, to which line 35 routes every write.
Every header's first sentence lists what SKILL.md holds without Revising these rules; not false (no 'only'; it defers to the table of files, which lists it, and the same header's 'Sections by file' line names it).
Row 77 lists §0, Every run leaves the record better organised than it found it, as owed for any number, while item 21's note owes none of the upkeep: the old text already routed every write to the upkeep (row 75) with the same carve-out in item 21's note and in the upkeep's own text; the item's note governs.
The H1 labels '§7, finding and writing' (research.md) and '§7, changing what the record says' (changes.md) leave Editing an existing page in the first file; labels only - both 'This file holds' lines and the table of files place it correctly.
SKILL.md line 102's dash list and items.md's '§0 ... - the numbered items' heading do not name Before any of this has ever been run or When a heavy pass is actually due; neither says 'only', and the table and the items header name both.
'Leave it closed otherwise' (files block) beside the record.md rule two sentences later is a stated exception; covered by round 1's set-aside of that rule.
Rows 67 and 75 say '§0 the upkeep every run owes' where the table of files uses the title; it resolves through the files block's '§0's upkeep', which stays in view after compaction.
The file map is repeated in the 'Sections by file' line of every header as well as the table: a maintenance cost for a reviser, not a breach of either of the skill's text rules (it glosses no rule's content and counts no list).
changes.md's Availability row says 'the pick' without its own §6 pointer; neighbouring rows of the same table carry (§6, Reaching a recommendation); unchanged old text.
Mechanical sweep: every titled §0 pointer and every titled §7 pointer (the short '*Revisions*' included) in every file resolves through the table of files to the file holding its subsection; every above/below, 'this section', 'the block', 'the next paragraph' and 'this band and the next' in the new files lands in its own file; no bare cross-file subsection title beyond round 1's two; bare (§0)/(§7) pointers and nicknames left as round 1 set them aside.
